newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CTP buys Solchem assets.
newsitem.headline: CTP buys Solchem assets.

text.p: South Africa's Solchem Investment Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that it had sealed a deal for CTP Holdings Ltd to buy its Solchem (PTY) Ltd unit for 54.2 million rand at 130 cents a share.
The deal with CTP, which owns 79.8 percent of Solchem, will see Solchem become a cash shell and give it nine months to acquire new assets or be delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
The deal will also see Plascon buy Solchem (Pty)'s liquid and sheet-fed printing inks operations for 25.6 million rand while Solchem (Pty) will buy Plascon's web ink operations for 3.1 million rand.

He declined to expand on what the deal meant for Solchem other than what the company itself had said -- that it would either become a cash shell with nine months to acquire new assets or be delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
At the moment Solchem's share price was looking a little inflated and could come back a little further on the day, dealers added.
"I think it's overshot the market somewhat and could come back a little bit later. It will probably find a comfortable trading range between 180 and 200 cents," one dealer said.

CTP was last steady at 51.25 rand with a meagre 500 shares trading in two moves.
